Earlier, 404 Media reported a vulnerability in the iCloud+ "Hide My Email" feature that could potentially allow anyone to obtain a user's real email address. Apple has now stated that the issue has been officially fixed.

Apple says the "Hide My Email" security vulnerability was patched earlier this month

If you're an iCloud+ or Apple One subscriber, Apple's "Hide My Email" privacy feature is particularly useful for protecting your real email address.

According to Apple's official website, here's how this feature works:

However, according to 404 Media's latest report, "Hide My Email" has long had a vulnerability that could allow anyone to obtain the real email address linked to an Apple account. This disclosure has also triggered a new recommended lawsuit.

However, Apple stated today that the vulnerability was officially fixed earlier this month.

Apple told 404 Media that the company "released a fix on July 3, and indicated that the issue was fully resolved."

The iCloud+ vulnerability was first reported by Tyler Murphy to Apple in June 2025. After initial communication, Apple claimed it had fixed the issue, but Murphy found the problem still existed. Hopefully this time it can be truly and completely resolved.

How often do you use the iCloud+ "Hide My Email" feature? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
